summary: The list stage's pagination size and timestamp format are whatever the live public API currently enforces, and a regen must re-probe them rather than trust a generic default. Two are load-bearing: the page-size cap (30 at the time of writing; anything above it is rejected outright) and the requirement that every temporal filter be a UTC 'Z' RFC3339 timestamp, since a local-zone numeric offset is rejected as an invalid date. Route every timestamp through a single helper so a new call site cannot reintroduce the offset form, and keep --db reaching the domain store rather than only the generic one.
reason: The generated defaults were guesses — page_size 100 against an API that caps at 30, and time.RFC3339 over a local-zone time — so sync-api could never complete a single page against the real service; the command had never worked. A fresh print restores those guesses, which is why the durable instruction is 'verify against the live contract', not the two numbers themselves.
validated_outcome: Probed live: page_size 30 succeeds and 31 returns HTTP 400; the UTC Z form is accepted where the local-offset form returns 'Invalid date'. A regression test pins both and names the probe results so the values cannot drift back silently.
